subject: Q3 usage signal & term flex for scale-up
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Claire Wu <claire.wu@nebuladata.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 usage signal & term flex for scale-up

Hi Claire —

Quick note after pulling your Q3 usage trends. Your app increased inference traffic 2.7x month-over-month in August (driven by a personalization rollout) and we see a persistent 14% week-over-week growth for September so far. Key highlights from the attached Q3 report:
- Total tokens (Q3-to-date): 1.9B tokens; avg token churn per inference: 760
- Median p50 latency: 78ms (redwood-hosted model variant); 95p latency: 320ms during peak windows
- Prefix cache hit rate improvement after recent SDK change: 42% (saves ~18% per-token cost on dialogue flows)

Given the traction, we think there are three practical paths that keep costs predictable while preserving performance:
1) Modest committed tier increase (proposed +40% monthly commit) — lower unit pricing and guaranteed burst headroom
2) Keep current commit + burst credits for seasonal peaks (short-term cheaper, but uncertain economics if growth sustains)
3) Multi-quarter ramp with a staged commit + canary (start with a 20% commit uplift, scale to 60% over 90 days)

I attached a pricing sketch and the usage CSV. Ben has modeled the ROI for each path below; we can walk through tradeoffs on a quick call. If procurement needs standard terms (SOW, PO timeline, or DocuSign), loop them in and we’ll push a clean DocuSign package.

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync early next week to pick a path and lock pricing or burst cadence. Does Tue 9/18 at 10am PT work for you?

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Growth
Redwood Inference

Hi Claire —

I pulled a compact pricing breakdown and an operational plan to make the uplift low-friction. Short version (numbers are monthly averages using current run-rate and projected 30-day growth):

Option A — +40% commit (start immediately)
- Base commitment: $48,000/month (was $34,000)
- Unit price (per 1k tokens): $0.85 (vs $1.05 on current plan)
- Estimated monthly overage at current growth: ~$6.2k
- Ramp benefit: immediate cheaper unit economics; requires PO + updated DocuSign amendment

Option B — Burst credits (no commit change)
- One-time 500k credit bucket: $9,500
- Unit price unchanged; best for 60–90 day seasonal spikes
- Risk: if growth sustains, credits deplete and overages accumulate

Option C — Staged ramp (20% -> 60% over 90 days)
- Initial commitment: $40,800/month; Step-up to $73,200/month
- Unit price floor negotiated at $0.88 per 1k tokens once at 60% commit
- Operationally we recommend a canary: route 20% of traffic to committed capacity for 14 days, monitor latency and cost delta, then step-up if stable

Operational notes:
- We can provision dedicated headroom in your region (us-west) and set autoscaling buffer for peak hours (midnight UTC rollover for your user base).
- We’ll enable a 3% discount if you accept a 12-month term extension tied to the commit uplift (standard enterprise addendum).

I uploaded the detailed spreadsheet to HubSpot and attached the compact proposal PDF. If these figures look reasonable, we’ll prepare a DocuSign amendment with the PO terms you provide.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive

Thanks for the clear options. Procurement prefers Option C (staged ramp) to reduce cash exposure while preserving the lower unit price once scale is proven. Before we proceed we need: 1) a copy of your SOC 2 Type II report and 2) the DocuSign amendment draft showing effective date language (we typically require a 30-day lead if escalation impacts invoicing).

Requested timeline:

- SOC2 package uploaded to our shared S3 link (or a secured portal) by Tue 9/18 EOD

If Redwood can meet the upload timeline, we’ll route internal approvals and target an initial 20% uplift to go live on Mon 9/25.
